findings.title: Timely response and compelled lowering
findings.claim: The pericope makes the focus's fall a timely response: belief in the signs takes bodily form when their bearers are reminded, while the earlier lowering and plea to return follow forgetting and belated sight and hearing.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers yu'minu, dhukkiru, and kharru meet 32:12's HFT-attributed head-inversion and late claim to see and hear, plus 32:14's forgetting. That contact places prostration after reminder beside a later lowered posture after missed remembrance, changing the reading from low posture as a self-sufficient sign to a response whose timing and cause matter.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's prostration is newly legible as an answer to reminder; the similar geometry in the judgment scene can mark compelled recognition after delay.
findings.containment: The recorded before reading is 'Falling low is intrinsically the sign of faith'; its after reading is 'Faith is timely, praise-bearing self-lowering; the same geometry without timely remembrance can instead mark compelled defeat.' The focus still says that those who believe in the signs fall prostrating, praise their Lord, and are not arrogant. This is a bounded contrast, not a claim that posture alone proves faith or that the earlier scene displaces the focus; the context can also be read simply as a contrast of outcomes. Context roots and roles from the legacy HFT remain attributed.

findings.title: Worship unfolding into release
findings.claim: The immediate continuation opens the focus's prostration and glorification into a repeated release: bodies leave beds, call on their Lord in fear and hope, and let received provision go outward.
findings.mechanism: The focus's prostrating and glorifying words are the carriers; 32:16's bodily movement away from beds and its spending are the independent triggers. Their contact turns the focus scene from a self-contained posture into the first point in an embodied practice that also releases comfort and provision.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus's low posture as the beginning of active devotion that moves from the body into how provision is used.
findings.containment: The recorded before reading is 'The focus describes a self-contained ritual moment'; its after reading is 'Its prostration is the first instance of a wider habit of release: from bed, from defensive stillness, and from retained provision.' The focus still describes prostration and praise. The movement-and-livelihood branch is a contextual resonance through the following ayah, not a lexical translation of Form II glorification; 32:16 can also be read as a list of distinct devotional practices. The HFT root and role assignments for context words remain attributed.

findings.title: Belief within an attachment topology
findings.claim: The later believer/fasiq contrast lets the focus's belief read, by contextual resonance, as secure attachment to the signs: refuge for believers and repeated attempted exit and return for the fasiq make fitting and slipping out perceptible as an interpretive topology.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier yu'minu can carry the supplied trust/security facet; the independent context carriers are the HFT-attributed image of a fruit leaving its skin, the refuge in 32:19, and the repeated exit/return in 32:20. Their contact with the focus's belief-in-signs phrase turns the moral contrast into a bounded image of secure fitting against separation and forced return.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the believer/fasiq distinction as more than paired labels: the surrounding destinations and movement make attachment, refuge, and separation newly visible together.
findings.containment: The recorded before reading is 'Believer and transgressor are two moral labels distinguished by conduct'; its after reading is 'The focus believer is one who remains securely fitted to the sign's sheltering order; transgression can be pictured as slipping out of the containing relation.' The focus still speaks of belief in the signs, and 32:18-20 still plainly contrasts moral groups and their outcomes. The attachment topology is an exploratory inference from legacy HFT roles; the alternative reading keeps fasiq as an ethical category and treats the refuges and fire as outcomes only. The context branch roots and roles are attributed, not independently lexically established here.

findings.title: Nontransactional praise as an inference
findings.claim: As an exploratory counter-image, the focus's prostration and praise meet the next verses' received provision, spending, and recompense: the sequence can be read as praise and giving directed to the Lord outside a tribute-for-acclaim exchange.
findings.mechanism: The focus words sujjadan and bi-hamdi rabbihim are the carriers. The qualified root branches for poll tax and favor-claiming are evoked only as analogical poles; the independent triggers are 32:16's provision received and sent outward and 32:17's recompense. Their contact makes the focus's praise and the believers' giving look like return to the Lord rather than a purchase of human acclaim.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive worship and spending together as a relation to the giver of provision, while the transactional comparison remains an explicitly bounded possibility.
findings.containment: The recorded before reading is 'Praise follows submission as devotional speech'; the HFT after reading is 'Exploratorily, the sequence rejects a tribute-for-acclaim economy: received provision circulates outward, while praise is returned to the Lord rather than purchased for the self.' This is not a lexical reading of either focus word. The qualified poll-tax branch is source-limited to other forms and expressly excludes prayer prostration; the favor-claiming branch is a specific collocation, not ordinary praise of God. The legacy HFT asks for an anti-transactional contrast, but plain devotion, generous spending, and promised recompense remain fully readable without that analogy.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and context Arabic anchors and listed word indices are supplied, but the anti-transactional relation is an HFT outlier from a legacy_unbound source. Its two focus branches have qualified, form-limited records and are retained analogically; unresolved context branches remain attributed.
